To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
haplo-insufficency of p53 is due to reduced p53 mRNA and that the p53 stress responses are attenuated in cells with a reduced level of p53.

loss of one wild-type p53 gene copy in HCT116 cells reduces p53 mRNA and p53 protein levels by four-fold, and that this reduction results in attenuated p21waf and survivin expression and reduced G1 checkpoint and apoptotic responses to oncogenic stress.

(1) loss of one p 53 allele results in 25% reduction in p53 mRNA and 40% reduction in p 53 protein levels; (2) p53 haploinsufficiency is manifested in attenuated p 53 stress responses; and (3) this is due to reduced p21waf 1 upregulation, survivin downregulati on, and G1 arrest and apoptotic responses to stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which p53 regulates the cell cycle, apoptosis and DNA repair.
the molecular and cellular biology of the tumour suppressor gene p53 and its role in the cellular response to stress.
the molecular basis for p53 tumour-suppressor haplo-insufficency.

p53 haploinsufficiency is due to reduced levels of p53 protein.
the haplo-insufficency of p53 is due to the reduced expression of p53 mRNA, and this reduced expression results in reduced protein expression.

the loss of a single p53 allele results not only in a reduction in protein levels but also in a reduction in the expression of the p53 gene itself, and that this reduction in gene expression is the primary cause of haplo-insufficency.

loss of a single p53 allele leads to four-fold reduction in p53 protein, and this is sufficient to explain why loss of a single allele is associated with a significant reduction in the tumour-suppressive function of the p53 protein.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the loss of one allele of a gene that encodes a protein with multiple functions (like p53) can lead to reduced levels of the protein, which may result in an attenuated response to stress, and ultimately lead to tumorigenesis.
